actuation: Dual-stimuli stiffness regulation: Joule heating of an embedded polyimide heating layer controlled by a relay and K-type thermocouple, and vacuum pressure (-0.1 MPa) applied via an external air pump and valve.

Soft gripper actuation: Tendon-driven mechanism powered by stepper motors (Hanpose 17HS8401) with motor drivers (EmbedFire BH-MSD4805) and active/passive gear transmission controlled by an STM32 microcontroller.
constitutive_assumptions: Shape memory polymer (SMP) is assumed to be linear, isotropic, and elastic under small deformations and low temperatures, with Young's modulus approximated by the storage modulus.
The HVS sandwich structure is assumed to behave as a cohesive beam under vacuum pressure prior to interlayer slippage.
Silicone rubber in the soft finger is treated as linear elastic up to 100% strain with an approximate Young's modulus of 0.038 MPa.
The three-point bending loading fixture is assumed to be an ideal rigid body in finite element analysis.
Stiffness contributions of the polyimide heating layer and polyethylene sealing envelope were neglected in the initial normalized analytical stiffness comparison.
control_variables: SMP layer dimensions (120 mm x 20 mm x 1 mm) and polyimide heating layer dimensions (100 mm x 20 mm x 0.25 mm).
Three-point bending span distance (48 mm) and loading/unloading speed (10 mm/min).
Ambient room temperature during baseline testing and natural cooling (approximately 25 °C).
FEA mesh element type (C3D8R 8-node linear brick with reduced integration) and seed spacing (0.3 mm).
dependent_variables: Load-bearing capacity / reaction force at 6 mm deflection (N).
Storage modulus and loss tangent tan(delta) of the SMP.
Dynamic friction coefficients between SMP and contact materials.
Temperature rising rate (°C/s) and natural cooling rate (°C/s).
Soft gripper payload capacity (g) and grasping stability across various object geometries.

evidence_relevant_to_topic.claim: The hybrid variable stiffness structure achieves a 15.7-fold bending stiffness range (0.31 N/mm to 4.86 N/mm) and a 16.0-fold load-bearing capacity range (1.76 N to 28.1 N) between State 1 (75 °C, 0 MPa) and State 4 (25 °C, -0.1 MPa).
Under identical temperatures, vacuum-activated layer jamming enhances bending stiffness by a factor of 1.60 ± 0.30 and load-bearing capacity by 1.39 ± 0.15.
SMP storage modulus decreases dramatically from over 1260 MPa at room temperature (~25 °C) to 2.8 MPa at elevated temperatures (>70 °C), with a glass transition temperature around 50 °C.
FEA explicit simulation demonstrates that bending stiffness decreases from 12 N/mm to 4 N/mm as deflection increases due to progressive interlayer frictional slippage.
The maximum heating rate reaches 2.77 ± 0.16 °C/s at 2 A, while natural cooling rate is -0.14 ± 0.05 °C/s, and jamming evacuation occurs within 1 millisecond.

Soft gripper fingers reinforced with Kevlar fibers and embedded with HVS structures resist buckling instability under high actuation forces, securely grasping objects ranging from 40 mm to 190 mm and lifting payloads up to 650 g.
Analytical formulation expresses bending stiffness scaling as proportional to temperature-dependent Young's modulus and pressure-dependent moment of inertia: K proportional to E(T) * I(P).
Hysteresis loops enlarge as temperature increases and vacuum pressure is applied due to SMP viscoelasticity and interlayer frictional sliding.

experimental_setup: Dynamic Mechanical Analysis (DMA 850, TA Instruments) on SMP film specimens (30 mm x 6 mm x 1 mm) from -20 °C to 120 °C at a heating rate of 5 °C/min.
Tribometer platform (TRB3, Anton Paar) measuring dynamic friction coefficients between SMP and PP, PDMS, and 304 stainless steel.
Mechanical test stand (ESM303, Mark-10) conducting three-point bending tests with a 48 mm span, 10 mm/min loading rate, and 7 mm maximum deflection.
Thermal characterization setup utilizing an infrared thermography camera and K-type surface thermocouple under electrical currents from 0.6 A to 2.0 A and natural cooling at 25 °C.

Three-finger soft gripper test platform equipped with tendon actuation, step motors, and interchangeable HVS structures to evaluate grasping of various objects (football, glass tank, cup of water, produce).
future_work: Integrating a barometer into the jamming system to achieve continuous and precise control of vacuum pressure.
Developing more accurate analytical mechanical models of the multi-layer HVS structure.
Investigating active cooling mechanisms or equipment to enhance cooling efficiency and phase transition speed.
Performing comprehensive characterization and modeling of hysteretic behavior.
independent_variables: Temperature / heating current (25 °C to 75 °C; electrical currents from 0.6 A to 2.0 A).
Vacuum pressure state (atmospheric 0 MPa vs. vacuum -0.1 MPa).
Loading/unloading rate during cyclic hysteresis testing (10 mm/min).
Grasped object physical properties (dimensions from 40 mm to 190 mm, weights from 2.7 g to 650 g, varied geometry and compliance).
limitations_inferred: Tethering dependency on external hardware (vacuum pump, DC power supply, motor drivers) limits self-contained mobile robotic deployment.
Thermal operation up to 75 °C may cause thermal degradation to surrounding elastomer matrix over extended cycling or damage heat-sensitive targets.
Long-term cyclic fatigue life and wear of the SMP contact surfaces under repeated jamming slippage cycles were not evaluated.
Energy consumption required to maintain the elevated temperature compliance state was not quantified.
limitations_stated_by_authors: Natural cooling rate is relatively low (-0.14 ± 0.05 °C/s) due to the lack of dedicated cooling hardware.
Vacuum pressure regulation was limited to binary on/off switching (0 or -0.1 MPa) rather than continuous regulation due to the lack of an integrated barometer.
Analytical modeling omitted stiffness contributions from the polyimide heating layer and polyethylene sealing envelope, leading to theoretical discrepancies above 45 °C.
Hysteresis characterization was preliminary and requires more comprehensive study.
main_results: The HVS structure demonstrated a 15.7-fold bending stiffness range (0.31 ± 0.013 N/mm at State 1 to 4.86 ± 0.11 N/mm at State 4).
Load-bearing capacity increased 16.0-fold from 1.76 ± 0.21 N at State 1 to 28.1 ± 1.76 N at State 4.
Layer jamming independently produced a 1.60 ± 0.30 times increase in stiffness and a 1.39 ± 0.15 times increase in load-bearing capacity at constant temperature.
SMP storage modulus transitioned from over 1260 MPa at ~25 °C to 2.8 MPa at >70 °C, with a glass transition temperature around 50 °C.
Dynamic friction coefficients for SMP were measured as 0.407 ± 0.043 against PP, 0.448 ± 0.024 against PDMS, and 0.485 ± 0.038 against 304 stainless steel.
Maximum heating rate reached 2.77 ± 0.16 °C/s at 2 A, natural cooling rate was -0.14 ± 0.05 °C/s, and jamming evacuation occurred within 1 ms.
Finite element analysis accurately captured progressive interlayer slippage causing tangent bending stiffness to drop from 12 N/mm to 4 N/mm under deflection.
A tendon-driven three-finger gripper utilizing HVS mechanisms prevented buckling under high tendon loads, grasping fragile objects and handling payloads up to 650 g.
modeling_methods: Theoretical analytical formulation: Bending stiffness scaling model relating temperature-dependent modulus and pressure-dependent moment of inertia, K proportional to E(T) * I(P), and soft finger composite bending stiffness calculations using K = E * I.

Finite Element Analysis (FEA): 3D nonlinear explicit dynamic simulation in ABAQUS/Explicit using C3D8R 8-node linear brick elements (0.3 mm seed spacing), rigid body contact for the loading fixture, and surface-to-surface penalty friction contact formulations based on experimental friction coefficients.
performance_metrics: Bending stiffness range (N/mm) and ratio between extreme states.
Load-bearing capacity (N) at 6 mm deflection and force variation ratio.
Stiffness enhancement ratio attributable strictly to layer jamming at fixed temperatures.
Thermal rate of change (°C/s) during Joule heating and cooling.
Maximum gripper lifting payload (g) and grasped object dimension range (mm).
possible_gap_implications: Combining material phase change with geometric reconfiguration demonstrates that jamming structures can achieve large stiffness ratios without bulky multi-layer stacks, addressing a key trade-off in soft actuator design.
The lack of continuous pressure regulation points to an opportunity for developing proportional-pressure jamming controllers to realize continuous variable stiffness gradients.

Discrepancies observed between simplified analytical beam models and experimental data above the glass transition temperature highlight the need for multi-layer composite models accounting for non-negligible encapsulation and flexible heater layers.
paper.research_objective: To design, model, fabricate, and experimentally evaluate a compact hybrid variable stiffness (HVS) mechanism synergistically integrating shape memory polymer phase transition and layer jamming, and to validate its performance in an articulated soft robotic gripper capable of versatile and load-bearing grasping.
paper.research_problem: Soft robots exhibit inherent low stiffness, leading to poor stability, low anti-interference capability, and restricted force output. Existing variable stiffness approaches—material phase transition (MPT) and geometric reconfiguration (GR)—fail to achieve miniaturization and fast response while maintaining a wide range of stiffness variation.
paper.robot_type: Soft robotic gripper (tendon-driven, three articulated fingers with Kevlar fiber reinforcement) / continuum variable stiffness fingers.
stiffness_mechanism: Material phase transition (MPT) via 4D printed shape memory polymer (SMP) layers with thermally tunable Young's modulus controlled by Joule heating.
Geometric reconfiguration (GR) via layer jamming (LJ) of SMP layers and an internal polyimide heating layer enclosed in an airtight envelope controlled by vacuum pressure.
paper.title: A Novel Hybrid Variable Stiffness Mechanism: Synergistic Integration of Layer Jamming and Shape Memory Polymer
